topics.topic: Result when multipart length subtraction is negative or inconsistent
questions: What result is passed to `migration_import` when the declared request length is smaller than the measured head plus the required closing delimiter, conflicts with the bytes actually exposed by the HTTP server, or cannot describe a complete final delimiter?

What is the file part's declared length when the request declares a total length smaller than the measured head plus the expected closing delimiter, or otherwise makes the subtraction negative or inconsistent with the streamed body?

What result does upload_framing produce when the request's declared length is smaller than the measured head plus the required closing delimiter, or otherwise cannot yield a non-negative file-part length?

quotes:
and the file part's declared length — the request's declared length less
the head it read and the closing delimiter with its final `--` and line end,
or none when the request declares none — so that a file of exactly the
import limit is not refused for its framing (A19 rule 4).
judgement.why: This is the same malformed or inconsistent multipart-length arithmetic question judged in P1, and the relevant passage has not changed.

precedent.topic: Exact multipart length arithmetic and handling of malformed or inconsistent framing
quotes:

the head it read and the closing delimiter with its final `--` and line end,
or none when the request declares none — so that a file of exactly the

precedent.why: Exact multipart byte arithmetic, delimiter syntax, epilogues, additional parts and malformed framing are encoding and contract questions belonging to State 6, not State 3 module ownership.

topics.topic: Concurrent arrival ordering and the rule for updating session last_request
questions: How are concurrent header-arrival readings ordered and applied when their session checks acquire the session lock in a different order, including whether `last_request` is assigned, advanced by `max`, or processed strictly in arrival order?
When concurrent requests arrive in one order but acquire the session lock in the opposite order, must `last_request` be assigned the processed reading or updated to the maximum arrival reading?

quotes:
At its arrival a request carrying a valid session restarts the session's
30 minutes, whatever its answer — a CSRF refusal included; of concurrent
arrivals the latest counts (A13 rule 2). A sign-out's admission marks the
session signed out at once.
judgement.why: The later owner-session operation explicitly makes the latest concurrent arrival count, so an earlier reading processed later cannot move last_request backward.

topics.topic: Exact request-arrival timestamp boundary and the module responsible for observing it
questions: Which module observes the exact completion of header reading and invokes the clock read, given that `owner_interface` is assigned the reading but the HTTP server and connection belong to later `instance_lifecycle`, which `owner_interface` may not know?
Is the reading taken when header reading begins, when the complete header block has been received, or at another precisely defined boundary?

quotes:
A request's arrival is the monotonic reading taken when its headers are read,
before any of its body, handed on for the session check (A13 rule 2).
judgement.why: The text assigns the clock observation to owner_interface and defines arrival at the point when the headers have been read, before body reading.

topics.topic: Required multipart structure and handling of malformed or missing closing delimiters
questions: Must an accepted upload contain exactly the CSRF part followed by exactly one final file part, and what are the required part names and headers and the treatment of extra parts, an epilogue, a missing final delimiter, or conflicting part headers?
What must the stream do if the closing multipart delimiter is absent, malformed or truncated after a syntactically valid head?

quotes:

judgement.why: P1 already judged the same questions about extra parts, epilogues, delimiters, and malformed multipart framing, and the passage has not changed.

topics.topic: Whether loopback plain HTTP is an exception to HTTPS-only cookie transport
questions: Is the cookie required to work on loopback plain HTTP, or is it forbidden from being accepted or sent on every plain-HTTP connection as “always HTTPS-only” states?
Is the cookie forbidden over every plain-HTTP connection, or is loopback plain HTTP an explicit permitted exception?

quotes:
The session cookie
is always HTTPS-only (A13 rule 1, owner, 2026-11-17): a browser on Registry's
own machine accepts it from a loopback address over plain HTTP, and from any
other machine the interface is reached only through HTTPS (R0-29).
judgement.why: This is the same secure-cookie and loopback-HTTP question judged in P3, and the quoted passage has not changed.

topics.topic: Whether session admission must occur before reading the multipart body head
questions: Must `owner_sessions.admit_owner_request` receive and apply the arrival reading before `upload_framing` reads the multipart head, or may the head be read first and the earlier reading supplied only afterward?
Must owner_interface invoke the owner_sessions admission check before reading any body, or may it read the upload head first and later check the session using the saved reading?

quotes:
Every request is checked at its arrival, and only then — at the arrival
reading it carries, however long its upload's head took to read after it: a session that has
reached 8 hours from sign-in or 30 minutes without a request, or is marked
signed out, serves no request; a change carries the CSRF value of its
session, compared in constant time (A13 rule 5).
judgement.why: The later owner-session operation requires admission at arrival before the upload head is read.

topics.topic: How the declared length and unread stream are passed to migration_import
questions: Through which module and capability do the declared length and unread stream reach migration_import, given that owner_interface does not list migration_import under Knows?

topics.topic: Whether authentication and concurrency reviews must be reopened for the A13 changes
questions: Because the same change set alters A13's request-arrival and session-validity timing, must the reopened review also record review of authentication_credential_abuse and concurrency, both of which name A13, or is the text asserting that A13 did not change?

topics.topic: Whether request admission survives later session expiry or sign-out without revalidation
questions: Does the header-time session check create an admission that retains everything needed to finish the request after the session is removed by the expiry pass or sign-out, or is validity checked again after the body head and CSRF value have been read?

quotes:
Validity is
   checked when a request arrives (A04 rule 6, stage 1); a request that
   passes it completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs, and
   a restart that interrupts it leaves nothing of it (A04 rule 4).
judgement.why: A13 explicitly says that a request which passes the arrival check completes without another validity check despite later expiry or sign-out.
